source_text:
Καλοὶ καὶ οἱ ἱερεῖς, κρεῖσσον δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς ὁ πεπιστευμένος τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, ὃς μόνος πεπίστευται τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ θεοῦ: αὐτὸς ὢν θύρα τοῦ πατρός, δἰ ἧς εἰσέρχονται Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ καὶ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ἀπόστολοι καὶ ἡ ἐκκλησία. πάντα ταῦτα εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ.
ἐξαίρετον δέ τι ἔχει τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ σωτῆρος, κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὸ πάθος αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν. οἱ γὰρ ἀγαπητοὶ προφῆται κατήγγειλαν εἰς αὐτόν: τὸ δὲ εὐαγγέλιον ἀπάρτισμά ἐστιν ἀφθαρσίας. πάντα ὁμοῦ καλά ἐστιν, ἐὰν ἐν ἀγάπῃ πιστεύητε.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, urging unity around the bishop and contrasting the old authorities with the gospel of Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Good [are] also the priests, but better [is] the high priest, the [one] entrusted [with] the holy [things] of the holy [places], who alone has been entrusted [with] the hidden [things] of God: he himself being [the] door of the Father, through which enter Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and the prophets and apostles and the church. All these [things are] for [the] unity of God. But something exceptional has the gospel: the coming of the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, his passion, and the resurrection. For the beloved prophets proclaimed [pointing] to him; but the gospel is [the] completion of incorruption. All [things] together are good, if in love you believe.

choices.why: ἀπάρτισμα means a finished work or completion; ἀφθαρσία is incorruption, not merely immortality, preserving the noun's force
καταγγέλλω with εἰς indicates direction or reference; the prophets' proclamation aimed at Christ

choices.term: ὁ πεπιστευμένος τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων
choices.english: the one entrusted with the holy things of the holy places
choices.why: τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων is a fixed phrase for the inner sanctuary; keeping the genitive construction preserves the temple reference
rejected: the one entrusted with the holy of holies
the one entrusted with the most holy things

choices.why: ἐξαίρετον means taken out, hence exceptional or surpassing; the indefinite τι is preserved

pass_b_english: The priests are good, but the high priest is greater. He is the one entrusted with the Holy of Holies, and he alone is entrusted with the hidden things of God. He is the door of the Father, and through him Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and the prophets and the apostles and the church all enter. All these things lead into the unity of God.

The gospel has something exceptional: the coming of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, his passion, and his resurrection. The beloved prophets proclaimed these things, pointing to him. But the gospel is the completion of incorruption. Everything together is good, if you believe in love.

last_rejected.why: Greek means 'completion that is incorruption' or 'perfecting unto incorruption', not 'of incorruption'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπάρτισμα ἀφθαρσίας is a genitive construction; 'completion of incorruption' is a valid rendering of the relationship.

polish.changed: Clarified that the high priest is Christ by making him the explicit subject of the following clauses, removed the dash for smoother reading, and adjusted the final sentence to avoid implying the prophets themselves were the gospel's completion.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.quote: the priests are good, but the high priest is better
notes.why: Ambiguous: are these Jewish priests, Christian presbyters, or Christ? Reader cannot place them.
notes.fix: Add a note clarifying the referent (likely Jewish priests vs. Christ as high priest).

polish.changed: Clarified that the high priest is Christ, not a Christian cleric, by keeping the contrast with the priests and making the pronoun references explicit; smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.quote: The priests are good, but the high priest is better
notes.why: Sudden introduction of 'priests' and 'high priest' without explanation; likely refers to Jewish priests vs. Christ, not Christian clergy.
notes.fix: Note these are Jewish/OT categories, not Christian offices.

polish.changed: Clarified the high priest as the subject of the door imagery, smoothed sentence flow, and made the contrast between the prophets' proclamation and the gospel's completion clearer.

notes.quote: The priests are good, but the high priest is better than they are
notes.why: 'Priests' seems to refer to Jewish priests or Christian ministers; context suggests Old Testament priests as types.
notes.fix: Note: Old Testament priests are types of Christ the high priest.

problems.quote: The priests are good, but the high priest is better
problems.why: Sudden introduction of 'priests' and 'high priest' without explanation; likely refers to Jewish priests vs. Christ, not Christian clergy.
problems.fix: Note these are Jewish/OT categories, not Christian offices.

edits.old: The priests are good, but the high priest is better.
edits.new: The priests are good, but the high priest is better than they.

fixed: The English already says exactly what the source says: 'The priests are good, but the high priest is better.' The source itself does not explicitly identify these as Jewish or Old Testament categories, so no change is needed.
